chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Abī Ṭālib, from Sadīr, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام): “There is a people who claim that you are gods, and they recite to us Qur’an for that:”
“And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God in the earth.”

So he said: “O Sadīr, my hearing, my sight, my skin, my flesh, my blood, and my hair are disavowed from these people, and Allah is disassociated from them. These are not upon my religion nor upon the religion of my forefathers. By Allah, Allah will not gather me and them together on the Day of Resurrection except while He is wrathful against them.”
He said: I said: “And among us there are people who claim that you are messengers, and they recite to us Qur’an for that:”
“O messengers, eat from the good things and act righteously; indeed I am Knowing of what you do.”

So he said: “O Sadīr, my hearing, my sight, my hair, my skin, my flesh, and my blood are disavowed from these people, and Allah and His Messenger are disassociated from them. These are not upon my religion nor upon the religion of my forefathers. By Allah, Allah will not gather me and them together on the Day of Resurrection except while He is wrathful against them.”

He said: I said: “Then what are you?” He said: “We are the treasurers of the knowledge of Allah. We are the interpreters of the command of Allah. We are a people who are maʿṣūmūn. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has commanded obedience to us and forbidden disobedience to us. We are the conclusive proof over those beneath the heaven and above the earth.”

key_terms.آلِهَةٌ: gods; a false claim of divinity attributed to the Imams
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ: the conclusive proof; the decisive divine authority over creation
key_terms.بَرَاءٌ: disavowed; a declaration of complete dissociation from those beliefs
key_terms.خُزَّانُ عِلْمِ اللَّهِ: treasurers of Allah’s knowledge; custodians of divinely granted knowledge
key_terms.دِينِي: my religion; the true creed and path affirmed by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.رُسُلٌ: messengers; a false claim that the Imams were prophets or messengers
key_terms.مَعْصُومُونَ: infallible; protected from error and sin by Allah
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection; the day on which such people face divine wrath

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about people who claimed the Imams were gods or messengers?
ai.summary: This hadith firmly rejects exaggerated beliefs that deify the Imams or raise them to the rank of messengers. It defines their true مقام as the divinely appointed, maʿṣūm guardians and interpreters of Allah’s knowledge and command, whose obedience is obligatory while remaining distinct from divinity and prophethood.
